facts.heading: The human part still matters.
facts.body: As AI reshapes work, employers are paying renewed attention to communication, critical thinking, creativity, empathy, and other human strengths—and English and the humanities are part of that conversation.

facts.heading: English stands out at UNO.
facts.body: In 2024, English was among UNO’s five most specialized fields by degree concentration compared with the national pattern.

facts.heading: When everyone has access to the same AI tools, what sets your work apart?
facts.body: Voice. Judgment. Context. Creativity. Understanding people. Communicating something worth remembering. Those are some of the human qualities bringing English and the humanities into new conversations about work in the AI era.

facts.heading: English doesn’t lead to just one kind of work.
facts.body: English graduates in the UK move into education, marketing and PR, administration, arts and media, writing and translation, and many other fields. The common thread isn’t one job title. It’s what you can do with language, ideas, evidence, and people.
facts.source: HESA Graduate Outcomes data, reported by Prospects, 2024

universal.PER01_COFFEE: The coffee shop with a notebook was a pretty good clue, too. Give you somewhere to sit, something to think about, and apparently you’ll take it from there.
universal.PER01_LIBRARY: You chose somewhere deep in the library. An hour among the shelves with nowhere else to be? We can see the appeal.
universal.PER01_LAB: You chose the puzzle café with a mystery to solve. There are worse ways to lose an hour than having something interesting to figure out.
universal.PER01_EDITORIAL: You chose the room where something is about to be published. There’s something exciting about seeing ideas take their final shape—and maybe helping them get there. I’d stick around, too.
universal.PER01_CLASSROOM: You chose the small group having a surprisingly good discussion. Sometimes one good conversation really is enough to lose track of an hour. An hour well spent.
universal.PER01_OUTSIDE: And somewhere outside with something to read still sounds pretty ideal to you. Honestly, hard to argue with that.

callbacks.W02_BOOKS: People arguing about what a famous book actually means. You came prepared to have opinions. Respect.
callbacks.W02_ACCENTS: Accents, language stories, and people comparing how everybody talks. Apparently even dinner gets a linguistic subplot.
callbacks.W02_STORIES: You found the people swapping unbelievable true stories, pulled up a chair—and, wait, did you bring a notebook?
callbacks.W02_MIND: People debating why language changes across groups and generations. Light dinner conversation. Very normal. Very demure.
callbacks.W02_MENU: Somehow, your table turned dinner into a menu-redesign project. Nobody asked you to fix dinner. And yet, here we are. Please don’t tell me you removed dessert.
callbacks.W02_GOSSIP: You chose the gossip table. Academically useful? Debatable. Socially? Impeccable instincts.
